title: "I saved my address and it changed back"
intro: Support has dozens of tickets since Monday: customers update their shipping address, the page reloads, and the old address is back. Refreshing a minute later shows the new one. On Monday the team moved all read queries to the read replicas 'to take load off the primary'.

steps.prompt: On the primary, check how far behind each replica is.
expected_commands: psql -c "SELECT client_addr, state, replay_lag FROM pg_stat_replication;"
psql -c "SELECT client_addr, state, replay_lag FROM pg_stat_replication"
steps.hint: pg_stat_replication on the primary shows replay_lag per replica.

steps.prompt: One replica is 38 seconds behind. Find out why: look at what's running on 10.0.2.22.
expected_commands: psql -h 10.0.2.22 -c "SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS runtime, left(query, 60) FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active' ORDER BY runtime DESC LIMIT 3;"
psql -h 10.0.2.22 -c "SELECT pid, now() - query_start AS runtime, query FROM pg_stat_activity WHERE state = 'active' ORDER BY runtime DESC LIMIT 3;"
steps.fake_output:
pid  |    runtime     |                             left
-------+----------------+---------------------------------------------------------------
 22814 | 00:14:52.4410  | SELECT customer_id, sum(total) FROM orders GROUP BY customer_
 23001 | 00:00:00.0041  | SELECT * FROM addresses WHERE customer_id = 8812
steps.hint: pg_stat_activity on the replica, ordered by how long each query has run.

steps.prompt: A 15-minute reporting query is running on the same replica that serves the website, holding back replay. Confirm that the address page reads from a replica: check the app's database settings in the ConfigMap shop-config (namespace shop).
expected_commands: kubectl get configmap shop-config -n shop -o yaml | grep -i db
kubectl get cm shop-config -n shop -o yaml | grep -i db
kubectl get configmap shop-config -n shop -o yaml
steps.hint: Look for the read and write hosts.

steps.prompt: Reads straight after a write go to a replica. Make a user's reads go to the primary right after they write: set DB_READ_AFTER_WRITE=primary on deployment shop in namespace shop.
expected_commands: kubectl set env deployment/shop DB_READ_AFTER_WRITE=primary -n shop
kubectl set env deploy/shop DB_READ_AFTER_WRITE=primary -n shop

steps.prompt: Stop the reporting query on 10.0.2.22 from delaying the website's replica: cancel backend 22814.
steps.hint: pg_cancel_backend(<pid>) cancels one query without killing the connection.

resolution: Asynchronous replicas are always slightly in the past. Moving every read to them means a user who has just saved something can be shown the version from before the save. With lag of a few milliseconds it almost never shows; with a replica 38 seconds behind it looks exactly like 'my change didn't save'. Two separate causes combined. The design gap was reading your own writes from a replica: the fix is to send a user's reads to the primary for a short window after they write (or to always read just-edited records from the primary). The operational trigger was a long analytics query on a replica that also served the site: on a Postgres standby, a long query can hold back replay of incoming changes, so the lag grows. Give reporting its own replica. And monitor replication lag with an alert, because every read-replica design quietly depends on it staying small.
